title: Constraint-driven Prioritization for Hosted API + Model Lineup (Quarterly)
creator: Sophie Kim
description: Purpose: Produce a repeatable, constraint-driven prioritization framework for the quarterly Hosted API + Model Catalog planning cycle. This ticket captures the PM-level artifact that will be used to allocate limited serving capacity, schedule model on/offboarding windows, and surface trade-offs to stakeholders. Scope: - Define the constraint vectors (GPU capacity, latency tail SLO, token-cost budget, model compatibility across runtimes, and regulatory region constraints). - Build a scoring function that combines demand signal (traffic forecasts + customer cohorts), model fit (quality delta vs baseline), and operational risk (memory/quantization compatibility). - Produce a prioritized rollout schedule for Q2 model candidates, grouped into Cohorts A/B/C for canaries and staged rollouts. - Deliverables: prioritization rubric (spreadsheet + short doc), a one-page decision memo for execs, and the initial rollout calendar (per-region). Out of scope: model training/new model development, infra procurement (handled by ENG roadmap tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Rubric defined: constraint vectors and scoring weights documented
Prioritized list of ~30 candidate model/endpoint changes with cohort assignments (A/B/C)
Rollout calendar with canary windows, fallback routes, and estimated capacity delta per week
Stakeholder sign-off (Eng reliability lead + Solutions PM + Sales rep) captured in comments
A short simulation run (back-of-envelope) showing expected latency and cost delta per cohort

decisions: Use a three-factor scoring model: Demand * Model Delta / Operational Risk (weights: 0.45, 0.35, 0.20 initially)
Hard constraint: do not accept changes that increase 95th latency beyond SLA by more than 10% in stage canaries
Allocate a 12% capacity buffer for sudden demand spikes during rollout windows (cross-regional hedge)
Default rollback policy: automatic re-route to baseline model if error rate > 2% or latency P95 regresses > 20% vs baseline within 6 hours
risks: Model compatibility surprises (quantization/warmup) could push more candidates into Cohort C, reducing churn impact
Underestimated demand spikes during canaries could breach SLOs despite buffer
Stakeholder alignment friction if Sales/CS request ad-hoc fast-tracks (mitigated by defined SLA for fast-track requests)
Simulation fidelity: short simulation (back-of-envelope) may miss tail behavior — requires Eng validation with perf test harness
